provenance.instrument: City of Nanticoke Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 500 Zoning, adopted by City Council 6-3-1993 by Ord. No. 12-1993 and amended in its entirety 12-19-2012 by Ord. No. 15-2012, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 NA2405, City of Nanticoke (500-403.2A and the 'Lot of record' definition refer to the Recorder of Deeds of Luzerne County). The accessory dwelling unit rules (500-302, 500-305, the 'Dwelling, accessory unit (ADU)' definition and the ADU parking line in 500-1118) were added by Ord. No. 9-2025 of 6-4-2025, which is in the code. District uses and figures are text in Article V. The only attachment is the zoning map. Floodplain rules are in Chapter 267. New Laws: only Ord. No. 1-2026 (refuse fees)
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 12-15-2025.' New Laws: Ord. No. 1-2026 (2-4-2026, refuse, recycling and bulk item fees) only
checks: Accessory dwelling units are among the permitted accessory structures on residential lots. 'Any lot with a principal single-family detached dwelling unit may have one accessory dwelling unit' (500-305A, B(1))

An ADU is 'A smaller, independent dwelling unit on the same parcel as a single-family dwelling. The ADU may take various forms: a detached unit, a unit that is part of an accessory structure, such as a detached garage ... or a unit that is part of an expanded or remodeled dwelling' (500-203)
'No accessory dwelling unit shall be located in front of the front building line of the principal structure' (500-305B(2))

'No setback shall be required for an existing garage living area or accessory structure or a structure constructed in the same location and with the same dimensions as an existing structure and converted to an accessory dwelling unit' (500-305B(3))
'The square footage of an accessory dwelling unit shall be less than 70% that of the primary dwelling and no less than a minimum of 400 square feet of gross floor area' (500-305B(4))
Parking: two spaces for the single-family structure and one for the ADU (500-305B(5), 500-1118A)

Accessory structures attached to the house meet the house's area and bulk rules. Unattached ones in an R zone stand only in the rear or side yard, at most 'two stories or 18 feet, whichever is the lesser', at least 5 ft from the side lines and 5 ft from the rear line (10 ft where the rear abuts an alley). In other zones they meet the house's front and side yards and a 10 ft rear yard (500-302). Outside R zones the district's building height applies: 'The maximum height of any building shall not exceed 2.5 stories or 35 feet' in C-OP (500-510.5G), three stories or 40 ft in C-1 (500-505.5G)

In R-1: 'No existing single-family dwelling unit shall be converted into two or more dwelling units or into any nonresidential use in an R-1 Single-Family Residential District' (500-802.12). This conflicts with a unit that is part of an expanded or remodeled dwelling in R-1
Single-family detached dwellings are permitted in R-1, R-2, R-3, C-1 and C-OP (500-501.1, 500-502.1, 500-503.1, 500-505.1D, 500-510.1). C-2, C-3, I-1 and S-1 list no single-family detached dwelling
Two-family dwellings are permitted by right in R-2, R-3 and C-1 (500-502.1B, 500-503.1B, 500-505.1D(2))

R-1, R-2 and R-3 set a maximum residential density in sq ft per dwelling unit 'for detached single-family residential developments' (500-501.6H, 500-502.6H, 500-503.6H). Whether it counts an ADU is not settled

A use 'neither specifically permitted nor denied' goes to the Zoning Hearing Board and Planning Commission as a special exception, if 'similar to and compatible with permitted uses in the district' (500-324)

A nonconforming residential building may not be enlarged or altered to add dwelling units unless it fully complies with the chapter (500-906E, 500-907). 'No... area nonconformity shall be increased' (500-904). But when a house is a nonconforming use in a nonresidential zone, 'the proposed erection of an accessory residential structure shall be deemed exempt from classification as an expansion of a nonconforming use' (500-308). So in C-2, C-3, I-1 and S-1 a detached ADU on an existing house lot may be allowed, while a unit inside or added onto the house is not

Floodplain (Chapter 267): in the floodway, 'no encroachments, including fill, new construction, substantial improvements, or other development shall be permitted' unless an engineering analysis shows no increase in flood levels, and no new construction or development without a DEP permit (267-19A(1), (2)). In an AE area without a floodway, no rise of more than one foot is allowed, and no new construction or development may be within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of any watercourse 'unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection' (267-19B(2)(a), (b)). A new or substantially improved residential structure must meet Chapter 267's elevation rules. The 50 ft rule in 267-26B is only for structures holding dangerous materials
Variances: 500-1409.2 sets the usual findings and does not bar a use variance

'Dwelling, single-family, detached: A residential building containing no more than one dwelling unit' (500-203), and an accessory structure is defined as detached. This sits uneasily with an ADU inside or added onto the house, which the 2025 ADU definition allows
'Mobile or manufactured homes shall only be permitted in mobile home parks' (500-802.48, Ord. No. 9-2025)
A 100 ft setback from any watercourse 'for any form of development' (500-802.36)
On a corner lot in an R district the side yard on the street is 10 ft (500-312C). Enclosing an area already under roof is exempt from the yard rules (500-313A)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: City of Nanticoke Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-16. Read: Article III (500-301 to 500-324), Article IV, Article V (500-501 to 500-510.7), 500-802.11 to 500-802.14, Article IX, 500-1118, 500-1408 to 500-1409.2A(3), the 500-203 definitions of accessory structure, dwelling, dwelling accessory unit (ADU), dwelling unit, single-family attached and detached dwelling, multifamily dwelling, lot coverage and lot of record, the New Laws page and two code searches (ADU terms, floodplain). Not read: Article I, the other definitions (including any two-family dwelling definition, height and story), Article VI (special exception standards), Article VII, the rest of Article VIII, Articles X, XII, XIII and XV, the rest of Article XI and Article XIV, and Chapter 267 beyond the search results and 267-19 (read on 2026-11-16). 500-308, 500-904, 500-312C, 500-313A, 500-802.36, 500-802.48 and 500-510.5G are cited from quoted text.

term.note: 'A smaller, independent dwelling unit on the same parcel as a single-family dwelling.'

status.note: A permitted accessory structure on residential lots. 'Where a principal use and/or structure is permitted, there shall also be permitted upon the same lot an accessory structure' (500-302). A zoning permit

scope_by_use.note: 'Any lot with a principal single-family detached dwelling unit may have one accessory dwelling unit.' C-2 and C-3 permit only dwellings over or attached to a business, and I-1 and S-1 no dwellings. 500-308 and 500-305B(1) may still reach a detached ADU on an existing house lot in C-2, C-3, I-1 and S-1 (see districts in doubt)

status_outside.note: These districts do not permit a single-family detached dwelling. A house there is a nonconforming use, which may not be enlarged or altered to add dwelling units unless in full compliance (500-906E, 500-907). But 500-308 exempts an accessory residential structure on such a lot from counting as an expansion of the nonconforming use, so a detached ADU there is in doubt, not barred

path.note: A permitted accessory structure. A zoning permit from the Zoning Officer

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board. The usual findings. No bar on a use variance

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-2, R-3, C-1)
value.conditions: 'Two-family dwellings' are a permitted use in R-2, R-3 and C-1 (500-502.1B, 500-503.1B, 500-505.1D(2)). Lot 7,000 sq ft 'for a structure designed as two-family residential dwelling' in R-2 (width 70 ft) and 6,000 sq ft in R-3 (width 60 ft). C-1 sets no lot minimum. Two parking spaces for each dwelling unit (500-1118B)
value.note: A building of two units, not a unit added to a house. The code does not say how an existing house becomes a two-family dwelling

building_types.note: 'Any lot with a principal single-family detached dwelling unit'

value.condition: Only a lot with a principal single-family detached dwelling may have an ADU. A twin or townhouse ('single-family attached', one of two or more buildings with a party wall) does not qualify.
In R-1 'No existing single-family dwelling unit shall be converted into two or more dwelling units'. A unit made inside or added onto the house may be such a conversion.

disputed_by.note: Ord. No. 9-2025 lets 'Any lot with a principal single-family detached dwelling unit' have an ADU, including 'a unit that is part of an expanded or remodeled dwelling'. The later and more specific ADU rule may control over 500-802.12

value.condition: An ADU may not stand in front of the front building line of the house.

In an identified floodplain area (Chapter 267), a new or substantially improved residential structure must meet Chapter 267, including elevation. In the floodway, no new construction, substantial improvement or other development is permitted unless an engineering analysis shows no rise in flood levels and a DEP permit is obtained. In an AE area without a floodway, no new construction or development may be within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of a watercourse unless a DEP permit is obtained.

In C-2, C-3, I-1 and S-1 a house is a nonconforming use. It may not be enlarged or altered to add a dwelling unit unless it fully complies with the chapter, so a unit inside or added onto the house is not allowed there.
A detached ADU may not be a mobile or manufactured home. They are permitted only in mobile home parks.
Any form of development must be set back 100 ft from any watercourse.

districts_in_doubt.note: A house here is a nonconforming use. 'In cases when a residential structure is a nonconforming use, located in a nonresidential zone, the proposed erection of an accessory residential structure shall be deemed exempt from classification as an expansion of a nonconforming use' (500-308), and 500-305B(1) reaches 'Any lot with a principal single-family detached dwelling unit'. So a detached ADU on an existing house lot may be allowed. A unit inside or added onto the house stays barred (500-906E)

types_allowed.note: 'a detached unit, a unit that is part of an accessory structure, such as a detached garage ... or a unit that is part of an expanded or remodeled dwelling'. 500-305B(3) also names 'an existing garage living area'

max_sqft.note: No square foot cap. The cap is a share of the house

max_share_of_house.note: 'The square footage of an accessory dwelling unit shall be less than 70% that of the primary dwelling'. The code says less than 70%, so a unit of exactly 70% of the house does not qualify

min_sqft.note: 'no less than a minimum of 400 square feet of gross floor area'

value.what: an existing garage living area or accessory structure, or a structure rebuilt in the same place with the same dimensions, converted to an ADU

exempt_building.note: 'No setback shall be required for an existing garage living area or accessory structure or a structure constructed in the same location and with the same dimensions as an existing structure and converted to an accessory dwelling unit or to a portion of an accessory dwelling unit.'

internal_uses_district_height.note: 'Accessory structures which are attached to a principal structure shall comply with the same area and bulk requirements which are applicable to the principal structure.'

setback_side_ft.note: Unattached accessory structures in R zones. On a corner lot the street side takes the front yard (500-304)

setback_rear_ft.note: Unattached accessory structures in R zones

setback_rear_alley_ft.note: 'when the accessory structure abuts an alley, 10 feet shall be required'

front_yard_barred.note: Unattached accessory structures in an R zone 'shall be erected only within the rear or side yard', and no ADU may be 'in front of the front building line of the principal structure'

accessory_cap_binds_adu.note: 500-305A lists the ADU among residential accessory structures, so the accessory structure height rule reaches a detached ADU

spaces_required.note: 'Accessory dwelling unit: one space for each accessory dwelling unit.'

total_on_site.note: 'Single-family structure: two spaces for each dwelling unit', plus one for the ADU

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: 'Maximum residential density: 8,500 square feet per dwelling unit for detached single-family residential developments.' Whether it counts an ADU on a house lot is not settled

max_building_coverage.note: 'Not more than 35% of the lot area shall be covered with buildings or structures'. 'Lot coverage' counts all buildings, including covered porches and accessory buildings (500-203)

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.note: 'two stories or 18 feet, whichever is the lesser' for unattached accessory structures in R zones

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling. Width 60 ft. 7,000 sq ft and 70 ft for a two-family structure

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: 'Six thousand square feet per dwelling unit for detached single-family residential developments.' Whether it counts an ADU on a house lot is not settled

max_building_coverage.note: 'Not more than 50% of the lot area shall be covered with buildings or structures'. 'Lot coverage' counts all buildings, including covered porches and accessory buildings (500-203)

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.note: 'two stories or 18 feet, whichever is the lesser' for unattached accessory structures in R zones

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling. Width 50 ft. 6,000 sq ft and 60 ft for a two-family structure

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: 'Five thousand square feet per dwelling unit for detached single-family residential developments.' Whether it counts an ADU on a house lot is not settled

max_building_coverage.note: 'Not more than 60% of the lot area shall be covered with buildings or structures'. 'Lot coverage' counts all buildings, including covered porches and accessory buildings (500-203)

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.note: 'two stories or 18 feet, whichever is the lesser' for unattached accessory structures in R zones

setback_front_ft.note: 'Minimum front yard: None.' 5 ft more where the district abuts a residential district (500-505.5H)

accessory_setback_front_ft.note: Unattached accessory structures outside R zones meet the principal front and side yards, which C-1 sets at none

accessory_setback_rear_ft.note: 'shall have a rear yard of at least 10 feet'

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.note: 'three stories or 40 feet' (500-505.5G). 500-302B sets no height for unattached accessory structures outside R zones, so the district's building height applies

max_building_coverage.note: 'Not more than 25% of a lot shall be covered by buildings.'

accessory_setback_front_ft.note: Unattached accessory structures outside R zones meet the principal front and side yards

accessory_setback_rear_ft.note: 'shall have a rear yard of at least 10 feet'

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.note: 'The maximum height of any building shall not exceed 2.5 stories or 35 feet' (500-510.5G). 500-302B sets no height for unattached accessory structures outside R zones, so the district's building height applies
